text:
mina: heads-up: QA found subtle hallucination spikes when we push fp8 for short-burst prompts (<=50 tokens). pattern: bursts of high confidence on wrong facts around token 20-30. anyone seen this?
ryan: saw similar in a customer-run yesterday. hypothesis: per-channel scale estimators fluctuate on short ctx, causing effective temperature drop and overconfident logits.
divya: agreed. also noticed that bias folding interacts poorly with per-head scales in some layers. folding pushes distribution toward extremes when scale estimate is unstable.
mina: can we add a lightweight temporal smoothing on scales (a tiny EMA across recent requests per shard) instead of instant swap? cheap and might fix noise.
divya: yep, propose: runtime keeps a small ring buffer of last 8 scale vectors per worker, compute median-of-means, use that when batch<6. avoids cross-request cold-start.
ryan: sounds promising. need to be careful about stateful behavior for private deployments and multi-tenant hosts. must be opt-in per-model or per-tenant.
mina: good point. default off in hosted for privacy reasons; enable only when `quant_stability_mode: "sticky"` is set in model config or via admin flag.
divya: we should also add a hysteresis guard so we don't flip precision too often: require N consecutive unstable decisions before switching precision, and a cooldown window to avoid thrash.
ryan: suggest params: unstable_count=2, cooldown_ms=2000, sticky_window=8. we'll tune.
mina: quick pseudo: ```py
scale = compute_scale(tensor)
if batch_size < 6:
  smooth = ringbuf_median_scale(worker_id)
  effective_scale = smooth if cv(scale) > 0.2 else scale
else:
  effective_scale = scale
# if effective_scale indicates instability increment counter, else reset
```
divya: also need telemetry tags: `quant.stability.cv`, `quant.switch.reason`, `quant.alpha_ema` and per-request `precision_pin` so we can see customer-level cost impact.
mina: rollback criteria for canary: if top1 factual accuracy drops >1.5% on the seeded eval set or if cost increases >10% for customers using sticky mode.
divya: add unit tests that simulate hot/cold start sequences and KV-cache warmup. small-batch warmups were a root cause too. include a test that replays shadow logs.
ryan: ops: will you add deploy note? deploy-bot: deploy: canary/quant-sticky v1 rolled to shadow at 09:07 UTC with tag `quant.sticky=true`.
divya: action items: mina implement ring-buffer smoothing + hysteresis; ryan add tenant opt-in and admin flag; divya write tests + telem; ops to run 48h shadow bench. schedule sync next Tue.
mina: adding doc blurb for runtime config: `quant_stability_mode: ["off","sticky","aggressive"]`, default off. sticky uses smoothing+hysteresis; aggressive uses conservative fallback to int8 for batch<4.
ryan: +1. we'll instrument cost tradeoff dashboard before broad rollout.
deploy-bot: reminder: PR template at https://git.redwood/infra/quant-stability has checklist and canary script. :rocket:
